active_discussions.sentiment: Enforcement after journalism; some channels already scrubbed by owners.
key_quotes: After a review, we terminated 20 channels — including all 13 referenced in this article and seven related channels — for violating our spam policies.

active_discussions.sentiment: Clips recirculate; killing source channels does not clear the shorts.
key_quotes: Terminating the source channels does not clear the clips. Riddance documented dozens of TikTok accounts recirculating moments from the long-form videos.

data_points.claim: A Backstage / Virelox-linked listing offered about $26 per video, 24-hour turnaround, actor supplies camera and lights.
Riddance AI tracked the network to more than 45 million YouTube views and 90,000+ comments, plus millions of TikTok plays.
YouTube told Semafor it terminated 20 channels (13 named + 7 related) for spam and deceptive practices.
Putting a real face in front of an AI script defeats synthetic-media detectors built to catch fake faces.
The cited violation was spam, not a public determination that each political claim was false.
Terminating source YouTube channels does not clear recirculated clips on TikTok.

common_questions: If the face is real, how is it AI content?
Did YouTube take them down for lying or for spam?
Are the TikTok versions still up?
Is this foreign influence or just ad-revenue farming?

misconceptions.myth: YouTube already catches AI video because of synthetic-media labels.
misconceptions.reality: The network used real hired hosts. Detectors looking for fake faces missed them.

misconceptions.myth: Taking down the YouTube channels deletes the campaign.
misconceptions.reality: Riddance documented TikTok accounts recirculating the same moments.

misconceptions.myth: This is a campaign op or a foreign intel op.
misconceptions.reality: Semafor describes engagement-for-ads growth hackers; Chan denied political clients. The videos still targeted Democratic figures.

audience_insights.knowledge_level: Shorts viewers have seen talking-head 'news' clips. They have not heard the $26 rate or that takedown was for spam.
pain_points: Rage-bait talking heads all look the same

research_summary: This week's actual YouTube/TikTok news is not a dance trend — it is a ghost-creator network that bought 45 million views with $26 actors reading AI scripts, beat fake-face detectors, then lost 20 YouTube channels after Semafor published. The clips are still hopping to TikTok. That is the 30-second short.
